web_evidence.title: A Column of Fire — authorized first-chapter PDF
web_evidence.note: The author's site supplies eleven continuous pages from Part One, sustaining external third-person narration of Ned throughout the chapter opening.

web_evidence.title: A Column of Fire Character Analysis
web_evidence.note: The detailed whole-book study identifies Ned as narrator of recurring, sporadic first-person segments; combined with the dominant third-person narrative it establishes a multi-person structure.

web_evidence.title: A Column of Fire Prologue-Part 1 Summary & Analysis
web_evidence.note: Structural analysis identifies the prologue narrator as Ned speaking in first person and separately analyzes the ensuing Part One narrative, corroborating the transition between narrative persons.

web_evidence.title: Follett, Ken Writing Styles in A Column of Fire
web_evidence.note: The whole-book point-of-view analysis identifies the dominant narrative as third-person limited following numerous focal characters; its broad description omits rather than disproves the short Ned interludes.

web_evidence.title: Review: A Column of Fire
web_evidence.note: A reviewer of the unabridged book independently notes first-person asides by Ned between sections, corroborating their recurrence and structural placement.

person_note: The novel's dominant narrative is third-person limited across multiple focal characters, as shown by q01644, q01651, q01653, the authorized Part One excerpt, and whole-book structural analysis. It also contains recurring autonomous first-person interludes narrated retrospectively by Ned, represented by q01643, q01648, and q01649 and explicitly identified by Tier B structural research. Because these are repeated base sections rather than speech, documents, or an isolated thought, the methodology requires ALTERNATING. The main residual uncertainty is the precise placement of some clipped Goodreads sentences, but it does not affect the independently established two-person structure.
